The predicted benefit is less draft work during ragged or partially occupied traffic, with little benefit when both counts select the same graph. H20 results motivate testing but do not predict H200 gains: acceptance changed, adaptive verification was enabled, and TTFT regressed at one reported load.

card.statement: Test coordinated prefill release only if measured mixed-step interference survives tuning the existing scheduler and static prefill interval. PR #61834 supplies a concrete per-step coordination protocol, but its reported interactivity gains come from an earlier MI355X branch and include substantial TTFT penalties; PR #51199 reinforces the need for a static comparator. Adapt the policy to each DP4 replica with MBT16384 and add an agreed wall-clock escape so protected decode periods cannot indefinitely postpone expensive chunks. Keep the CPU collective implementation fixed during this experiment. The prediction is fewer disruptive mixed steps, not an automatic throughput gain; promotion requires a better TTFT/TPOT frontier after accounting for queueing and coordination overhead.

credible_improvement_required.rationale: Coordinating prefills can plausibly reduce repeated lockstep decode interruption. The proposal first checks existing alignment and compares static prefill intervals plus separately labeled MBT tuning, satisfying the baseline-relative mechanism requirement. Unmeasured mixed-step exposure is an appropriate first falsification question.

h200_applicability_and_correctness_requi.rationale: The host protocol is plausibly adaptable to fixed DP4/EP4, but installed scheduler compatibility and the proposed overdue mechanism are unverified. The source excludes elastic EP and custom schedulers. A wall-clock flag checked once per step can override HOLD decisions; it does not by itself establish a hard request-wait bound during long steps, repeated chunks or resource starvation.

discriminating_experiment.rationale: Static-policy controls, fixed offered schedules, unfinished-request accounting, collective overhead and release-reason counters directly address competing explanations. Held-out long chunks and idle-to-active waves are useful. The design appropriately treats an unresolved TTFT tradeoff as inconclusive. Specify request-versus-chunk age, deadline-check cadence and attainable wait guarantees before qualification.

traceable_engineering_support.rationale: The engineering PR describes the six-int FIRE/HOLD protocol and reports "No GPU runs on this branch yet." Earlier results are author reports from DeepSeek-V4-Pro on MI355X DP8, not this Flash/H200 deployment; at concurrency 64, TTFT rose from 3.76 to 8.63 seconds for little total-throughput change. The supplied packet lacks the implementation diff, and #51199's benchmark hardware is unknown.

practical_value_and_portfolio_coverage.rationale: Mixed agentic traffic is relevant, and screening static settings first limits wasted integration effort. This remains the most complex scheduler intervention, with substantial TTFT risk and no supplied production tradeoff. Its value is conditional research value, not established deployment suitability.

objections: Name DeepSeek-V4-Pro explicitly as the source model; the reported results do not measure V4.1-Flash.
The wall-clock escape is a new adaptation whose progress semantics need specification.
Earlier-branch results, cross-node comparisons and CPU simulations cannot establish the submitted branch's serving behavior.
The treatment refers to h200-systems-002 rather than the current R2 identifier.

experiment.control: Attested allocation with matched NUMA placement and sorting. Include exact-size cudaHostAlloc as an attribution control and the strongest supported existing THP/placement configuration as a practical comparator.
experiment.correctness: Check exact table bytes and lookup outputs at shard and allocation boundaries, sorted/unsorted paths, empty and uneven batches, registration fallback, teardown and repeated allocation/free. Exercise graph replay and distributed storage lifetime. If outputs or math change unexpectedly, require numerical and quality qualification rather than acceptance statistics. Map relevant cases to G01-G05 once supplied.
experiment.cost: Cheap allocation inspection, then moderate allocator/lifetime validation. Host-memory savings are not GPU KV savings or an automatic node-price reduction. Use C8*T/(3600*Nqualified), with C8 unknown.
experiment.held_out_condition: Primary native agent-f75 and Mooncake at seq64. Hold out cold/warm allocation phases, long and ragged prefills, repeated versus random row IDs, and simultaneous memory pressure from both replicas. Keep random-row microbenchmarks separate.
experiment.inconclusive_if: Storage ownership, physical-memory accounting or registration telemetry is unresolved, host pressure is unrepresentative, or serving differences remain within drift.
experiment.metrics: Denominator: private offloaded table allocations eligible for exact registration; numerator: successful exact registrations, with fallback counts. Track logical bytes, actual registered bytes, physical host usage without double-counting shared mappings, faults, pressure and NUMA traffic. Measure lookup rows and exposed lookup time, TTFT tails, request TPOT, exact tokens, qualified goodput, KV/preemption, draft counters and replay lag on all ranks.
experiment.rejects_if: Tables are already exact/shared with no relevant delta; registration is unsupported; lookup gains remain entirely hidden; no serving value appears under adequately covered relevant conditions; or lifetime/correctness failures occur. Record memory-only savings separately.
experiment.supports_if: The eligible branch activates and reduces actual allocation waste; serving qualification additionally requires lower exposed stalls or lookup time and better unprofiled metrics than the strongest comparator. Confirm small effects with at least five alternating paired full-run blocks and held-out checks.
experiment.treatment: First inspect effective allocation and source presence. If eligible, change only exact-size registration and fallback handling; qualify before unprofiled serving tests.

card.mechanism: Source fix: reuse the registration helper without huge pages for exact-sized private offloaded tables, falling back on registration failure. card.observed_bottleneck: Unknown on H200. Author-reported GB10 TP4, 32K-token measurements reduced host allocation from 33.1 to 24.3 GiB with registration. Exact cudaHostAlloc used 24.9 GiB but retained the same 41.4 ms unsorted lookup time; registered storage reported 22.7 ms. End-to-end offload validation was still outstanding. These sizes and timings do not establish TP1/DP4 behavior.
card.predicted_direction: Lower physical host allocation if rounding exists; potentially lower TTFT or higher throughput only with demonstrable pressure or exposed lookup savings. Decode benefit and all H200 effect sizes are unknown.

Only for an eligible rounded private-table path, adapt #59849. Keep table values, sorting thresholds, partitioning and communication unchanged; do not bundle packed exchange or shared cuMem backing.

card.statement: Test exact-size registration of CPU-offloaded Engram tables only after resolving whether this deployment uses private DP shards or shared host storage. The launch arguments establish offload and embedding_across_dp, but do not establish allocation ownership, rounding or backing. PR #59849 separates two effects: exact sizing reduces host allocation, while registration type changes lookup performance in its GB10 experiment. If the live private-table path still rounds allocations, port that allocation change with safe fallback and unchanged sorting and NUMA placement. Compare against exact-size cudaHostAlloc and supported existing THP settings. Predict serving benefit only if host pressure or exposed lookup latency falls; memory savings alone do not establish lower H200 cost per token.

credible_improvement_required.rationale: The supplied code:h200:resolved-engram logs resolve "dp_shared_memory=True, use_thp=False" on both replicas. R5 explicitly targets rounded private tables and rejects shared storage. Its own cheap eligibility check therefore rules out the proposed delta as scoped. No change to the active shared-storage path is proposed.

h200_applicability_and_correctness_requi.rationale: Generic CUDA host registration is plausibly portable, but the proposed private-table intervention does not match the resolved shared-storage deployment. R5 preserves ownership and explicitly excludes the shared-backing alternative, leaving no remedy within this proposal. This is a deployment-path mismatch, not evidence that H200 cannot register host memory.

discriminating_experiment.rationale: The attribution controls correctly separate exact sizing, registration type, sorting and placement, and the rejection rules explicitly cover shared tables. The experiment is discriminating because the supplied configuration evidence already triggers its stop condition. A later shared-storage proposal would need a different activation denominator and comparison.

traceable_engineering_support.rationale: The GB10 TP4/32K lookup figures and "Exact size gives the memory saving; the registered memory type gives the speed" are accurately attributed author claims. However, describing shared-versus-private configuration as unresolved ignores the supplied resolved logs. Actual backing, physical bytes and H200 lookup effects remain unknown; those uncertainties do not restore private-path eligibility.

practical_value_and_portfolio_coverage.rationale: An ineligible private allocator port should not occupy one of five practical baseline improvements. Its inspection has useful exclusion value, but the proposed serving change has no identified active allocation target. Host savings would not automatically imply GPU KV savings or reduced node cost even in an eligible deployment.

objections: Both replicas resolve shared DP Engram storage; the draft's central deployment uncertainty is stale.
The proposal's own shared-storage rejection condition is met.
GB10 private-table timings do not establish behavior of the deployed shared-storage path.
Resolved shared mode does not establish whether the physical backing is /dev/shm or cuMem, its page mapping, or exposed lookup cost.
